cards.example: High inflation means that prices rise faster than wages, so people can afford less every month.
As a student I live on a tight budget, so I rarely eat in restaurants.
Consumerism encourages people to buy things they do not really need just to feel happier.
It is extremely stressful to be in debt, especially if you suddenly lose your job.
The cost of living in Budapest has risen so much that many students cannot afford to rent a flat.
Many pensioners can hardly make ends meet because food and energy prices keep going up.
It is hard to earn a living as an artist unless you become really famous.
Families with a low income spend most of their money on food, rent and bills.
Many people believe that the rich should pay higher taxes to fund schools and hospitals.
Banks rarely give a loan to young people who do not have a regular income.
If you borrow money from a friend, you should always pay it back on time.
I still owe my brother twenty euros because he paid for my cinema ticket last week.
Most young couples need a mortgage to buy their first flat, which they repay over many years.
When interest rates are high, it is better to save money than to borrow it.
I am trying to save up for a new laptop by working in a café at weekends.

cards.example: My grandparents lost most of their savings when their bank collapsed in the nineties.
Many small shops could go bankrupt if a huge shopping centre opens nearby.

Investing on the stock market can be risky, because share prices can fall suddenly.

Schools should teach financial literacy so that young people learn how to manage their money wisely.
Online advertisements encourage impulse buying, especially among teenagers who spend hours on social media.
I found a real bargain in a second-hand shop: a leather jacket for only five thousand forints.

cards.example: Expensive brands are not always good value for money, so compare prices before you buy.

cards.meaning: nem sajnálja a pénzt vmire, sokat költ vmire
cards.example: After my exams I am going to splash out on a weekend trip with my friends.

cards.meaning: erején felül él (többet költ, mint amennyit megengedhet magának)
cards.example: People who live beyond their means often end up borrowing money from friends or banks.
